60ca1d1fb2.q: Why did Tax Fitness choose the top 20% as the benchmarking threshold instead of comparing against average performers?
60ca1d1fb2.a: The philosophy stems partly from the Pareto principle, where 20% of clients drive 80% of profits. Tax Fitness uses the top 20% because statistics show 43% of small businesses in Australia are losing money, and another 20-30% make less than the average Australian wage of $120,000 with super. By benchmarking against the top 20%, businesses get achievable targets and incentive to improve from whatever percentile they're currently in.
60ca1d1fb2.rq: If you're serious, you've got to jump on the benchmarking train. If you're not doing that, what value are you adding?
ks: 43% of small businesses in Australia are losing money
Average Australian wage with super: $120,000
Plastering company subcontractor costs: 70% of turnover (benchmark: 40%)
Plastering company profit increase: from $200,000 to $1.5 million over two years
Accountant revenue increase per tradie client: from $1,000 to $10,000-$12,000 annually

37e1940e82.q: What were the seven key profit levers identified in the Tax Fitness benchmarking package?
37e1940e82.a: The seven key profit levers are: cost of goods sold, subcontractors, rent, wages, overheads, owners compensation, and net profit or loss. Darren emphasizes that most businesses typically turn on one or two main KPIs to improve, and the Tax Fitness approach focuses on identifying and fixing the single biggest problem first before moving to the next.

0385d5fe7b.q: What profit improvement did a plastering company achieve using Tax Fitness benchmarking over two years?
0385d5fe7b.a: A plastering company with $10 million turnover started with $200,000 annual profit. Their main problem was subcontractors costing 70% of turnover instead of the benchmark 40%, resulting in only 1-2% profit instead of 20%. Over two years, by focusing solely on reducing subcontractor costs, their annual profit increased to $1.5 million. The accountant charged $4,000 per month ($48,000 annually), earning $96,000 over two years while the client gained $1.3 million in additional profit.
